#!/bin/bash
 
#FLUX --queue=serial                   # Send this job to the serial partition
#FLUX -n 4                        # number of cores
#FLUX --time=12:00:00                  # wall time (D-HH:MM)
#FLUX -o slurm.{id}.out             # STDOUT ({id} = JobId)
#FLUX -e slurm.{id}.err             # STDERR ({id} = JobId)

# NOTE: The --mail-user and --mail-type directives have been omitted as Flux
# does not have a direct equivalent for job status email notifications.

module load gcc/4.9.2
module load matlab/2015b
cd /home/sliu104/MoCapGaussian/
matlab -nodisplay -nosplash -nodesktop -r "runMoCap_AA_AA_4()"

issues: The job requests 4 tasks via '#FLUX -n 4' but launches the `matlab` application as a single, serial process. Since the command is not prefixed with a parallel launcher like `flux run`, only one of the four allocated tasks will be used, leaving the other three tasks idle and wasting significant resources. If the MATLAB code is multi-threaded, the resource request should be changed to '#FLUX --ntasks=1 --cpus-per-task=4'. If the code is purely serial, the request should be '#FLUX -n 1'.

#!/bin/bash
 
#SBATCH -p serial                   # Send this job to the serial partition
#SBATCH -n 4                        # number of cores
#SBATCH -t 0-12:00                  # wall time (D-HH:MM)
#SBATCH -o slurm.%j.out             # STDOUT (%j = JobId)
#SBATCH -e slurm.%j.err             # STDERR (%j = JobId)
#SBATCH --mail-type=END,FAIL        # notifications for job done & fail
#SBATCH --mail-user=sliu104@asu.edu # send-to address

module load gcc/4.9.2
module load matlab/2015b
cd /home/sliu104/MoCapGaussian/
matlab -nodisplay -nosplash -nodesktop -r "runMoCap_AA_AA_4()"
